problem: Navigation benchmarks pose goals in the world the agent currently sees, and existing two-visit benchmarks (RoomR, EMQA, FindingDory) score recall or rearrangement, not navigation. None can express goals defined by a change, such as 'the chair that was moved' or 'where the vase used to be'.
motivation: Homes change between a robot's visits, and requests like 'put back the chair that was moved' refer to states that no longer hold. Current-state or self-maintaining open-vocabulary maps overwrite the past, so it is unclear whether they can answer past-tense queries at all.
key_idea: Define navigation to a goal selected by a cross-visit change relation (including vacated locations where nothing remains to detect) and release a benchmark of 219 two-visit AI2-THOR episodes, each certified solvable by an oracle that completes it three times.
insight: With oracle positions the two-visit agent reaches 0.995 static / 0.991 embodied, so the decision rules and navigation are not the obstacle. The error budget shows grounding costs only 0.064 of the gap, while mapping (localisation and cross-visit association) costs 0.516. Reading DualMap's maps as two visits does not recover FORMER/REMOVED (0.355 vs 0.365 overall, the maintained map is ahead on the past relations), so keeping a map current is not the whole obstacle. Adding appearance cues to the association cost leaves the multi-change split unchanged (0.676 to 0.671), which points to the missing instance identity across visits.
method: Task formulation: an episode is (scene, scripted change δ, query (category, relation)). Six relations (MOVED, FORMER, MOVING, STABLE, APPEARED, REMOVED) are predicates on two world states, and answers are current or past positions.
Anti-shortcut admissibility: the referent must be unique and every query category has n≥2 instances, so category recognition alone is at chance 1/n.

Success test: ObjectNav-style 1.0 m radius using distance to the object's bounding box and the nearest navigable cell, plus a visibility check for current-position answers. Past-position answers drop the visibility term since nothing is there to see. SPL is also reported.

Certified generation (Algorithm 1): a candidate is kept only if an oracle agent, given the true answer, completes it with the same primitives and test three times. Observations are checked against the evaluated world, and rejections are counted per query type.

Reference two-visit agent, perception and grounding: YOLOv8m-seg masks are back-projected with median depth and CLIP crop embeddings are clustered at 0.6 m into per-visit maps. Grounding keeps every instance within 0.03 of the best CLIP text similarity.

Reference agent, association and decision: Hungarian assignment with cost = distance + λ·feature disagreement, padded with dummies so gate γ=1.25 m. Rules use non-assignment as evidence (argmax distance among unmatched instances), with fallbacks or abstention, and MOVING uses the latest unmatched track cluster.

Navigation and baselines: A* on a grid recomputed after the change, with 0.25 m / 30° primitives and a 500-action budget. Compared against single-visit, CoW and DualMap (as maintained map and as two visits) baselines, with paired McNemar tests.

setting.backbone: YOLOv8m-seg + CLIP ViT-B/16 (frozen) with hand-designed association/decision rules; baselines CoW and DualMap
setting.training_data: none (training-free reference agent; pretrained detector and CLIP)
setting.observation: RGB-D + pose + instance masks along a fixed 6-waypoint x 4-heading tour per visit
setting.action_space: low-level primitives: forward 0.25 m, turn 30°, stop (500-action budget)
setting.privileged: none for the main arm; diagnostic arms are given ground-truth grounding or positions, and the agent is supplied the category and relation unless stated otherwise

numbers_note: OVMAN is a new benchmark with no official splits, so 'test' is used as a placeholder for the full 219 episodes. Per-relation values are stored under the paper's own short names.
results: The two-visit reference agent reaches 45.2% embodied SR (SPL 44.0) versus 28.3% for the single-visit arm and 12.3% for CoW, and beats CoW on 83 episodes to 11. The oracle-position variant reaches 99.1%, so the remaining gap comes from mapping and cross-visit association, not from grounding or answer selection. Reading DualMap as two visits does not recover past-position relations (overall 0.365 vs 0.355 for the maintained map).
limitations: Single scripted change per main episode, in one simulator (AI2-THOR) and 20 indoor scenes; the multi-change split is much harder (APPEARED 0.185).
Per-relation cells hold only 32-40 episodes, so per-relation differences are trends, and the embodied per-relation margins are mostly not significant.
The reference agent is not a proposed method: it is hand-designed, and cross-visit instance identity is left unsolved.
